note: One source, one curation tree: each native family carries one independent claim, separable by column, native subject and entry locator, so the claims share one prepare per step. Expected values are the replaced tests' assertions restated at the build boundary; a null provider key surfaces as unresolved_catalog_identity on the native family. Family 7: the replaced test also asserted a compiled ambiguity for `unknown`; no build output carries it. Family 9: `new` alone is valid, but a family's owners apply all or nothing. Family 10: the later of two owners of one (record, column) is the competing entry. Family 14: the loader refuses a map that owns no literal, so PP_OTHER gives the partition one owned literal, and the scoped PP_ID occurrence sits in its own variant (11) because a column owner selects by variant, column and edition.
fails_if: any one of: `compile_partitions` stops withholding an `[[identity.unassigned]]` family (5: `quantity` is published); `convert_column_partitions` moves a declared unassigned literal to the only owner (6) or withholds the family when one split name matches no literal (7), or cites a scoped-owned occurrence in `unassigned_original_columns` (14); the `partition has no active split naming` stale is dropped (8); the family applies its surviving owners when one is stale (9; `_scoped_column_owners` returning none and `compile_partitions` skipping a family with scoped-owner issues are two redundant guards, so only dropping both fails this) or lets a later owner overwrite an earlier one (10); `select_coding` treats a guarded `stored_role` like an ordinary uncoded entry (15, 16) or accepts an ordinary one over a complete list (17); `compile_enrichment` binds a partition owner's description by record instead of (record, column) (18) or checks the existing description on every record sharing the ref (19)
